A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FSU-QA/FSU-Bench study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–E support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original VLM evaluations, Qwen3-VL-8B fine-tuning results and experiments augmenting VLM inputs with Epona and DrivingWorld predictions.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and additionally reports counterfactual-label validation and a shuffled-prediction control experiment.

M1.justification: The QA pipeline, evaluation mappings in Equations 1–3, input combinations and fine-tuning procedure remain unchanged. The added geometric explanation of counterfactual annotation documents the existing rule-based approach without establishing an algorithmic revision.

E1.justification: The nuScenes coverage and nine tasks remain unchanged. Section 5.2 adds a test condition using future predictions from a different scene, introducing semantically mismatched input context. Waymo and nuPlan are mentioned as future directions, not evaluated datasets.

E2.justification: The same 13 baseline VLMs and two world models are evaluated, with unchanged comparator membership in corresponding appendix experiments. Llama's corrected classification in the prose does not change participation. The new benchmark-comparison table describes prior work rather than reporting additional baseline evaluations.

E3.justification: v3 adds protocols for auditing 150 counterfactual annotations and randomly replacing WM predictions with another scene's predictions. Existing splits, accuracy scoring and training settings remain unchanged; most newly prominent inference settings already appeared in v1 Appendix B.

E4.justification: v3 adds validation of both central benchmark components: expert verification of counterfactual labels and shuffled-future controls testing whether WM benefits depend on relevant semantic content. These substantially expand validity analysis beyond the retained modality comparisons, although the shuffled-control outcome is reported only qualitatively.

E5.justification: v3 first reports human–automated-label agreement and chance-corrected Cohen's kappa for the counterfactual audit. Benchmark scores still lack repeated-run variability, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: All seven model-results tables retain identical scores and rankings. New results include 89% annotation agreement, kappa 0.78, 654 revised or removed QA pairs, a final flagged-error rate below 5%, and qualitative accuracy decreases under shuffling. Section 5.1 also introduces an incorrect ranking claim: Claude-Sonnet-4.5's Risk Area score of 49.33 is called best among closed models, although Table 2 gives Gemini-2.5 Flash 54.67.

T1.justification: Equations 1–3 and their mathematical content are retained. The new counterfactual-validity discussion supplies geometric motivation and empirical validation, not a new formal definition, derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The dataset, joint evaluation and fine-tuning contributions remain. v3 sharpens novelty claims around semantic counterfactual reasoning versus immediate planning, qualifies WM evaluation as probe-dependent, and narrows demonstrated fine-tuning benefits to the nuScenes domain.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations involving pretraining-data scarcity and architectural differences, qualifies counterfactual validity by closed-world geometry, and explicitly acknowledges probe dependence and untested cross-domain generalization. The geographic-bias limitation already existed in v1 Appendix D.

D1.justification: v3 details quality control involving 45 scenes, three experts and three review rounds, and explicitly discloses single-pass inference without retries. These disclosures do not establish changes to existing experiments. Fine-tuning hyperparameters remain identical, while direct project and evaluation-code links disappear and the dataset link remains.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands positioning against driving VQA, planning and trajectory forecasting, including DriveLM, OmniDrive, NuScenes-QA and GPT-Driver, and adds a feature-comparison table. Several earlier world-model citations are removed. One new citation is mismatched: EMMA points to reference 49, titled Equivariant multi-modality image fusion.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, related-work narrative, several results discussions and conclusion are substantially rewritten. The separate Future Work section is replaced by directions within the conclusion, and author affiliations, acknowledgments and supplementary headings also change.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column layout to a single-column proceedings format, extensively resizing and relocating figures, tables and prompt boxes. A benchmark-feature comparison table is added. Existing plots and qualitative examples retain their content.

improvement.justification: The quantitative annotation audit, fuller curation documentation and clearer limits on proxy evaluation modestly strengthen v1's evidence and claim calibration. These benefits are constrained by the absence of numerical shuffled-control results, removal of direct code links, and newly introduced ranking and citation inconsistencies.
